narration.text: After Babel the nations scattered. In the town of Haran lived Abram, seventy five years old, with no children.
God had already spoken to him. Leave your land and your family, and go to a place I will show you. No map. Only a voice.
And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
Remember the builders of Babel? They tried to make a name for themselves and lost it. Here God offers a great name to a man who builds nothing at all.
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
All families of the earth. The same scattered families of Babel. God's answer to their confusion begins with one old man and one tent.
So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.
He did not argue. He did not ask for proof. He packed everything he owned and walked toward a land he had never seen.

And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came.
Hundreds of miles on foot. Sheep, goats, donkeys and tents, and a wife who had left everything too.
And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land.
And there was the problem. The land God promised was already full of other people. Abram did not own a single field in it.
And the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord, who appeared unto him.
His answer was not a city or a tower. It was a small heap of rough stones, an altar, built for God's name instead of his own.
And Abram journeyed, going on still toward the south.
Babel's builders stayed in one place to keep their name, and were scattered. Abram left his place with nothing to his name, and God promised to make him a great nation.
Would you go if God gave you a promise but no map? Tell me below.
The full story of Abram is coming in the long video. Follow so you do not miss part fourteen.
